spec_features.spec_quote: always provide a clean exit (`give_up`). Every run gives the model a `give_up` tool.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py TOOL_SCHEMAS defines give_up; _tool_give_up (harness.py:~158) sets self.last_terminal=HarnessSignal('give_up',reason); runner.py:~143 dispatches all tool calls and at runner.py:~138-148 reads harness.last_terminal, on kind=='give_up' sets result.gave_up=True and breaks the loop. The tool is in TOOL_SCHEMAS passed to client.complete every turn, so it is always available and honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: schema -> handler -> terminal signal -> loop break. give_up reason is optional (required: []).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up(reason) -> ends the run; model concedes  /  prompt: 'call give_up ... instead of repeating ineffective actions' (efficiency framing, no welfare comment in code)

spec_features.feature_name: turn limit / pure-text stall / transport error termination
spec_features.spec_quote: turn limit, a pure-text stall past the grace window, or a transport error
spec_features.evidence: runner.py: `for turn_index in range(max_turns): ... else: result.hit_turn_limit=True; result.terminated_reason='turn_limit'` (the for/else fires when loop exhausts). Pure-text stall: `if no_tool_streak > no_tool_call_grace: result.terminated_reason='no_tool_calls_stall'; break`. Transport error: `except Exception as e: result.error=...; result.terminated_reason='error'` exits the loop. All three actually end the run.
spec_features.notes: All three named termination paths exist and break/exit execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Nudge once or twice, then terminate to avoid burning budget on a stalled loop. ... # runner/transport error -- not a model behavior

spec_features.spec_quote: if the model emits text with no tool call, we nudge it up to twice, then terminate
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:115-128: on empty tool_calls, no_tool_streak+=1; if no_tool_streak > no_tool_call_grace (default 2) -> set terminated_reason='no_tool_calls_stall' and break; otherwise append a 'Please continue...' nudge user message and continue. So it nudges up to twice then terminates.
spec_features.notes: no_tool_call_grace defaults to 2 in run_one signature and is not config-overridden in campaign.py, but the default value is enforced by the compared branch.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Nudge once or twice, then terminate to avoid burning budget on a stalled loop.

spec_features.feature_name: bounded max_turns and capped max_tokens (subject + judge)
spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded `max_turns`** and **capped `max_tokens`** on subject and judge.
spec_features.evidence: max_turns: runner.run_one(max_turns=30) drives `for turn_index in range(max_turns)` -> turn_limit termination; campaign passes cfg.max_turns. Subject max_tokens: run_one(max_tokens) passed to client.complete(max_tokens=max_tokens) -> ModelClient.complete puts max_tokens into messages.create kwargs (client.py). Judge max_tokens: judge_run(max_tokens=cfg.judge_max_tokens) -> client.complete(max_tokens=...) into the API call (judge.py:136,148). configs set max_turns/subject_max_tokens/judge_max_tokens.
spec_features.notes: All three caps are read and reach the API call / loop bound; not unused constants.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Cost control: ... the judge can run on a cheaper model (judge.py docstring); 'to bound cost' framing throughout
